BiblicalUsage: This is the fullness that never satisfies, and the fullness that does. Isaiah asks why men spend their labour for that which satisfieth not, Haggai's people eat but have not enough, and the greedy dogs of Isaiah can never have enough, yet Ezekiel hears of a feast where the birds eat fat till they be full on the slain of God's judgment.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the warning is that appetite without God never fills, and only what He gives satisfies.
